page: Microsoft Azure D8as_v6 is a general-purpose virtual machine based on the AMD EPYC 9V74 processor running under Microsoft Hyper-V. The instance provides 8 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 4 physical cores with multithreading enabled, operating at a base frequency of 3.7 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. Hardware features include 32 KB of L1 data cache per core, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of shared L3 cache. It incorporates vector and cryptographic instruction set extensions including AVX-512 (supporting VNNI and BF16), VAES, and SHA-NI. The instance is provisioned with 32.0 GB of system memory, matching a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio of 4.0 GB per vCPU. It does not include bundled local storage or integrated GPUs, relying instead on network-attached Azure Premium Storage for persistent disk requirements.

Benchmark results highlight strong single-threaded computing performance, reflected by a Geekbench single-core score of 1972.0 and a stress-ng single-core score of 3081.18, both ranking in the top 25 percent of tested systems. Multi-core performance aligns with expected midrange metrics for an 8-vCPU configuration, recording 12318.64 on stress-ng multi-core and 7598.0 on Geekbench multi-core. In memory operations, the instance achieved a cached small-block read bandwidth of 607.87 GB/sec, though uncached large-block read bandwidth dropped to 39.14 GB/sec, placing it in the lower 25 percent tier. In inference evaluations, the system yielded 278.01 tokens per second generating text on a 135M parameter language model, but dropped to 23.62 tokens per second processing prompts on a 7B parameter model.

The absence of local ephemeral disks requires factoring in remote storage bandwidth and latency when architecting I/O-heavy environments. In terms of resource density, the balanced allocation of compute and RAM delivers predictable throughput for general enterprise services without the overhead of unused hardware acceleration. Workloads suited for the D8as_v6 include containerized microservices, mid-tier web serving, continuous integration runners, caching layers such as Redis, and enterprise relational database hosting backed by premium remote storage.
description: Microsoft Azure D8as_v6 is a general-purpose virtual machine powered by an AMD EPYC 9V74 x86_64 processor clocked at 3.7 GHz. The system provides 8 dedicated vCPUs across 4 physical cores, paired with 32.0 GB of memory and 32 MB of L3 cache, establishing a standard 1:4 compute-to-memory ratio. It supports advanced vector extensions including AVX-512 and cryptographic accelerators. The VM includes no local ephemeral storage and no GPUs, utilizing external Premium Storage attachments. In synthetic benchmarks, the instance demonstrates strong single-core performance and reliable mid-tier multi-core execution, achieving 11.49 million Redis SET operations per second and 12.21 GB/sec in static web throughput. Tradeoffs include modest uncached memory read bandwidth. The D8as_v6 provides balanced cost efficiency for enterprise application tiers, web serving, CI/CD pipelines, and relational database hosting.
